recruit_text.forward:
Every town in the Barrens with a fire brigade of its own, and he's started training the first one.

His mother, Inés, knowing he's alive. He writes her a letter every week and keeps them all.

stages.stranger: Hermano, I'm Cristóbal! I'm a firefighter, or I was, and now the fire lives inside me, which is very funny if you think about it. I go in first and I come out last, that's the rule.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Valparaíso, from the hills above the port, hermano. My father left when I was four, and my mother cleaned offices and raised me alone, and sent me off every morning with empanadas. I joined the forest fire brigade at twenty-three. Twelve years in the hills, on a motorbike that broke down every week, and I danced cueca very badly at every fiesta.
stages.companion: In 2024 the hills above my mother's house burned, and I spent four days on the line while the city burned below us. Her house was still standing when I came down. I'll never forget that. My mother is Inés. I haven't found her, so I write her a letter every week and I keep them all, in a sack, cachai.
stages.friend: On my first day here I landed in the middle of a grass fire in the Barrens. There were other people in it, people from Earth, and I was the only one who walked out. I've never stopped thinking about them. That's why I train the young tauren to cut breaks. The dry season's coming early this year, hermano, and something big is going to come at Taurajo. I need you with me on the line.
stages.sworn: The line held, and the kids held it without me for the last hour while I was pulling people out. They did it, not me. And then a letter came from across the sea. My mother's alive! She heard there's a crazy Chilean fighting fires in the Barrens and she knew it was me, and she told me to be careful. I sent her all the letters at once, three years of them, in a sack. She's going to be reading for a month.

moments.prompt: He's just told you about the grass fire on his first day.

options.text: You couldn't have saved them all.
options.reply: I know, hermano. My head knows. The rest of me is still in that grass.

options.text: Then let's make sure it never happens at Taurajo.
options.reply: Yes, hermano, that's it, exactly that. Let's go and cut some breaks.

moments.prompt: After the wipe he's laughing, too loudly, checking everyone over.
moments.line: Okay, okay, everybody's breathing, that's the main thing! We go back in, but smarter, hermano.

options.text: You're allowed to be shaken, you know.
options.reply: Ah, you noticed. Okay, give me a minute, then we go.
That's the spirit, hermano! Follow me in.

lines.bored_warning: Hermano, we've been burning the same field for days. Even fire gets bored. Let's go somewhere with a bit of excitement.
lines.leaving_good: That was a great trip, hermano! I'm going back to Taurajo to check on my brigade. Come and find me when you need someone to go in first.
lines.leaving_bored: I'm going back to Taurajo. Nothing's happening out here, and my kids need drilling.
lines.after_wipe: Okay, everybody's breathing! That's what matters. Now we go back in, but smarter.
lines.wipe_warning: We keep dying in here, hermano, and even I'm not laughing now. One more run, then I need a break.
lines.wipe_leave: I stayed until it was done. Now I'm going back to Taurajo for a while. Come and get me when you've got a better plan, cachai?
lines.zone_warning: Hermano, this place is a wildfire with the wind behind it. You don't fight that, you get out of its way.
lines.zone_leave: I'm stopping here. I told you it was a wildfire. I'll be at Camp Taurajo.
lines.gear_refuse: Ah, no, hermano, that one's mine. Ask me again when we've had a fiesta together.
lines.gear_taken: Take it, take it, I'm fireproof anyway, mostly.
lines.gear_short: I'm still missing that piece, hermano. I'm not complaining, just singing about it.
lines.gear_upgrade: Hermano, this is beautiful! Thank you! I'm going to dance in it tonight.
lines.back: I'm back, hermano! The brigade's drilled, the breaks are cut, and I'm ready. Where's the fire?
lines.send_word: Cristóbal has sent word from Camp Taurajo. His brigade's ready and so is he.
lines.walkout_talk: I left angry, hermano, and that's not me. Sit down, let me tell you why, and then you tell me, and then we eat.
lines.neglect: Hermano, there you are! I thought you'd forgotten me. I danced at three fiestas without you.
lines.asked_to_stay: Okay, one more, hermano! Then I check my brigade.
lines.on_break: Cristóbal is back at Camp Taurajo, drilling his fire brigade. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.
lines.quest_abandoned: We left those people waiting, hermano. In my job you never leave anyone behind.

town_arrive.text: Look at those roofs, hermano. One spark and the whole street goes. Somebody needs a firebreak.
My mother sent me off every morning with empanadas wrapped in a tea towel. I'd kill for one of those right now, hermano.

close_call.text: Too close, hermano! I'm going back in for you next time, don't argue.

dungeon_clear.text: Nobody's burnt and nobody's left inside, hermano. Back home this is when we'd put the kettle on.

zone_arrive.text: Can you smell that? It's dry grass. If this place goes up, it goes up fast.
